Interesting tale of how wonderful we all are now since slavery and Plantation life has ended in the Deep South. A family goes into a plantation home and freely fondles all the furniture and decorations (a display like this would have PROBABLY been roped off even then). We then get a highly odd flash history of how the plantation system worked. Although the whites vs slaves is briefly touched upon, this film unfortunately somewhat sugarcoats the relationship between Plantation owners and slaves. Heck, even when the plantation period has ended, there still seems to be some sugarcoating going on.

Fat-Assed Southern Colonel's Sitting On The Porch Sipping Mint Julep's , After Banging The House Darkies....While The Wive's Are At Tea...Mulatto's Running Amuck On Massa's Plantation....And Da Sun Keeps Shinin' Down...Ahh The Good Old South....Tells Me A Story Uncles Remus!....

Toni Morrison has characterized race relations in the US as depending on something she calls the "escape from knowledge." This film epitomizes the resistance to self-examination that often calls itself objective history. This is like what would happen if the Germans made a film about WWII in which they talked about how Hitler built the Autobahn and wondered where all the Jews went.

NASA_Launchpad_Biosphere_HD_: Visit Biosphere 2, operated by the University of Arizona, to find out how scientists are working with NASA to discover more about the effects of global climate change could have on key biomes. Learn about the characteristics that divide Earth into unique terrestrial biomes.
belmore-boat-to-africa: Ray and Virginia Garner celebrated their 1938 wedding with a trip to Africa, sailing from Bellmore, Long Island. Some or all of the sea footage in this film may have been shot on theirvoyage from Belgium to Africa. This home movie features Ray & Ginny; they play a net game together; Ginny in hay wagon; Ginny doing dishes; Ray rock climbing; Ray & Ginny leaving their house; ship to Africa; Ray & Ginny swimming, diving, cavorting in ship's small swimming pool; angry seas, crossing equator…
Fourfemaleacrobats-wellcome: Shows a variety of acrobatic movements to demonstrate the action of muscles, vertebral column, hip and shoulder joints in living subjects. Four female acrobats perform a variety of movements while interspersed radiograms show the spine in various positions. 5 segments.

rv: Funny episode of the popular 50's sitcom "Love That Bob". Will Bob win the heart of a swedish girl? Yes, The actress who plays Schultzy is the same actress who played Alice on "The Brady Bunch". She shows her great comic timing in her supporting role. I deduct one star for mocking Rock'N'Roll. Come on, Surely a show this hip should of known better? (And lets face it, "Love That Bob" was a pretty hip show). Still, This is a great sitcom!
Bob Digs Rock `N` Roll (The Bob Cummings Show).

Season 4, episode 33. Original air date: 27 May 1958. Bob tries to help Chuck win back his steady girlfriend, who has fallen for a teen- aged rock and roll perdormer. Cast: Bob Cummings (Bob Collins), Ann B. Davis (Charmaine `Schultzy` Schultz), Dwayne Hickman (Chuck MacDonald), Ingrid Goude (Ingrid Goude), Olive Sturgess (Carol Henning), Dan Tobin (Wally Seawell), El Brendel (Ole Svensen), Stanley Stenner (Stanley Stenner), Bill Baldwin (Announcer) and Nancy Kulp (Pamela Livingstone: Archive Footage). FRom IMDB.

The scientist is killed however by a gang of criminals, led by a woman named Mado, who wish to get the instructions for building the mechanical man. the-devils-circus-1926-by-benjamin-chris: The Devil's Circus is a 1926 silent drama film directed by Danish director Benjamin Christensen, based upon his screenplay. The film stars Norma Shearer and Charles Emmett Mack. It was the first of seven films directed by Christensen in the United States, and one of only four of those films that have not been lost.
bunny-maloney-dawn-of-the-shrimp-lost-ep: A timid man undergoes a personality change, and turns the tables on the people who've bullied him.
gov.archives.arc.25045.r7: Department of Defense. Department of the Army. Office of the Chief Signal Officer. 1916 War As It Really Is - Reel 7 7 Reels. Reel 7, Germans surrender, are marched to a stockade in the rear, and searched. Shows mutilated corpses, abandoned German war materiel, and French and U.S. trenches.
ssfSTRK1917: A strike begins at the Union Iron Works at the foot of Potrero Hill in 1917.
33-325-r2: CARRY ON Produced: 1930 Description Reel 1, 4-H club members sightsee in Washington, D.C. The members view the Declaration of Independence in the Library of Congress and visit Mt. Vernon. Reel 2, the boys and girls see exhibits in the Smithsonian Institution, a session of the House of Representatives, the Lincoln Memorial, and Arlington National Cemetery. President Hoover delivers a short address.
